title: Athar
summary: THE SCRIPT IS FRENCH. About the History of Islam & how Genghis Khan's children conquered one-fifth of the world. There's no footage of any of it, obviously, so every frame gets built. Which means every frame has to hold up when someone looks at it closely.
technical: The hardest part is researching the history. Even though the script is there, I still have to find out every bit of detail behind each scene. After fully grasping the story, I draft the entire episode in one sitting. Every cut, every scene, every map animation, the entire flow of the episode is decided beforehand. The next few days are just a grind of executing every scene and preparing every asset. The Art Director works on generating the scenes from scratch as planned in the narrative master map (the draft of the episode), while I build the timeline in parallel. With the score, bilingual subtitles from JSON, and the composition set up, we just wait. Then the assets come in, and each scene gets separated into layers across depth and rebuilt in 3D. That's where a still becomes a shot; camera movement, atmosphere, and effects are stacked in. Editing isn't the hard part; making the story is.
